saints.name: St. Clement Mary Hofbauer
saints.title: Priest, Redemptorist
saints.shortBlurb: A baker who became the first Redemptorist north of the Alps and the tireless “Apostle of Vienna”…
biography: Born in 1751 at Tasovice in Moravia, the ninth of twelve children, John Hofbauer was apprenticed to a baker at Znojmo and for years baked at the Premonstratensian priory of Louka, kept from the seminary by poverty and by the religious laws of the Emperor Joseph II.

Making his way to Rome, he joined the Redemptorists, taking the name Clement Mary, and was ordained priest in 1785, the first of the congregation professed north of the Alps. Sent to Warsaw in 1787, he made the church of St. Benno a center of daily preaching, confession, and schooling for orphans, laboring there for twenty-one years.

Expelled with his brethren by Napoleon's order in 1808, he settled in Vienna, where his pulpit, confessional, and direction of students and converts so renewed Catholic life that he is called the Apostle of Vienna. He died there on 15 March 1820 and was canonized by Pius X in 1909; he is patron of Vienna and, from his early trade, of bakers.
saints.knownFor: Planting the Redemptorists in northern Europe and reviving the faith in Vienna.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 15 March
